candidates.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (submitted 17 Nov 2026; project page released; reproducible materials promised upon acceptance)
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 3 天，Semantic Scholar API 429 rate limit 無法查得引用數；preprint 剛發布，實際引用數幾乎必為 0
communitySignals: HuggingFace Daily Papers 2026-11-19：33 upvotes，2 條留言
credibilityEvidence: Sec 3-4: formal variance decomposition (sigma=within-artifact noise, tau=run-to-run true-quality variance), 1,030 independent evolution runs, 2.1M test trajectories, 10M LLM calls, 7 methods x 6 models x 4+9 benchmarks
Sec 4.1 Table/Fig 2: single-run method ranking only picks the true-best of 4 text-artifact methods 33% of the time on Terminal-Bench (vs 25% random)
Sec 4.2 Fig 3: largest reported literature gains (median 17.6pp) collapse to median 0.8pp after repairing evaluation shortcuts; one audited sentence reproduces 90% of the original gain

Sec 5.2 Table 1: execution-based selectors and LLM judges all statistically indistinguishable from 50% coin-flip at picking the better of two candidate artifacts; regressions are 30.5% of pool but 62.1% of accepted candidates
Sec 5.3: in-loop validation gains (6.9-9.0pp) vanish under independent re-evaluation (+0.4 to -3.2pp)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: largest reproducibility study of agent evolution to date per the authors' own claim, with explicit statistical power analysis and null-model controls (equal-quality null, empirical-Bayes posterior); core finding replicated across method-level and candidate-level analyses independently
reproducibilityEvidence: project page live (https://lineshogan.github.io/resolution-hypothesis/); authors state full trajectory data/code released only upon paper acceptance, not yet public
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: claim is narrow and precisely scoped (evaluation resolution, not 'agent evolution is useless'), and every quantitative claim traces to a described experiment with variance estimates
candidates.primaryLimitation: code/trajectory data not yet publicly released (pending acceptance), so the headline numbers cannot yet be independently re-run by a third party
candidates.hiddenAssumption: the paper's own selection-failure diagnosis assumes its audited benchmarks (Terminal-Bench, SpreadsheetBench, OfficeQA, ALFWorld) are themselves representative of the evaluation regimes used across the wider agent-evolution literature
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: if atypical, the 33%/49.7% chance-level numbers would be benchmark-specific rather than a general property of agent-evolution evaluation; however the method-level finding (margins smaller than single-run noise) is replicated across 4 very different benchmarks and 7 methods, so the core claim would likely survive even a narrower reading
candidates.presentationReason: unusually explicit about what is established vs hypothesis, defines resolution formally, separates sigma/tau variance sources before making any claim
candidates.reason: largest-scale, most rigorously controlled evidence this round for a theme that recurs across three independent papers today: current agent evaluation practice cannot reliably tell real improvement from noise

candidates.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 10th MLSys Conference, 2027 (accepted, peer-reviewed systems venue)
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 2 天，尚無引用資料（Semantic Scholar API 429 rate limit；preprint/剛接受論文時間太短，引用數幾乎必為 0）
candidates.institution: Citigroup Inc. + Ernst & Young LLP + NVIDIA Corporation (all London)
communitySignals: 未見於 HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code
credibilityEvidence: Sec 4-6: nine-dimension capability taxonomy scored by cross-functional panel across 10 real agentic AI platforms (H2O.ai, Google, Microsoft, Writer, Letta, Glean, CrewAI, UiPath, Portia AI, Squid AI) on 3 financial-services scenarios
Sec 6.3: Cronbach's alpha=0.98 across 9 nominally distinct dimensions, rank correlation >=0.93 with total for 8 of 9 dimensions -- a quantified halo-effect test, not an assertion
Sec 6.4: tier structure checked for robustness under two alternative weighting profiles (governance-first, developer-first); tiers unchanged, only within-tier order shifts

Sec 7 Table 4: explicit Threats-to-Validity table covering presentation confound, halo effect, unequal panel size, ordinal-as-interval scoring, no ground truth for CCR scenario, vendor self-selection, single-institution scope, construct/temporal validity, vendor-reported cost/latency, absence of adversarial/safety testing
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: real industrial multi-vendor bakeoff with quantified reliability diagnostics, but explicitly scoped as demonstration-based (assisted vendor conditions) rather than hands-on controlled benchmarking
reproducibilityEvidence: scoring methodology, taxonomy and raw aggregate score table (Table 3) published; per-rater raw scores were not retained by the Lab, so inter-rater reliability cannot be independently recomputed (acknowledged by the authors)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: the halo-effect claim is a direct statistical test (alpha, rank correlations) on the paper's own data, not an inference stretched beyond what was measured
candidates.primaryLimitation: single institution, vendor-assisted demonstrations (not blind hands-on evaluation), and D8 cost/latency figures are vendor-reported rather than independently measured
candidates.hiddenAssumption: the nine capability dimensions are assumed to be conceptually independent constructs that a panel can score separately from a single demonstration; the paper's own alpha=0.98 result falsifies this assumption for the panel-based protocol as administered
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: this is the paper's central finding rather than an unexamined premise -- it explicitly shows the assumption fails and proposes how to fix the protocol, which strengthens rather than weakens the credibility case
candidates.presentationReason: formal protocol, explicit [established]/[documented]/[observed]/[proposed]/[hypothesis] tagging throughout the paper, full threats-to-validity table
candidates.reason: the only candidate today documenting how buyers (not benchmark authors) actually evaluate agent platforms, and the only one with a real peer-reviewed venue (MLSys 2027); its halo-effect finding generalizes the Resolution Hypothesis's point from automated self-improvement loops to human procurement panels

candidates.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
candidates.venue: KDD 2026 Workshop on Evaluation and Trustworthiness of Agentic AI (ETAAI), Jeju, Korea -- workshop presentation, non-archival
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 2 天，尚無引用資料（Semantic Scholar API 429 rate limit；workshop 剛發布，引用數幾乎必為 0）
communitySignals: 未見於 HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code（但程式碼與全部 1,445 筆 trial ledger 已於 GitHub + Zenodo 公開，DOI 已發放）
credibilityEvidence: Sec 5.1-5.2: 1,445 trials across 6 ML tasks (synthetic logistic regression, 2 OpenML tabular tasks, MLAgentBench vectorization, ResNet scientific trigger, GPT pretraining), 100% ledger provenance completeness on every node including a 120-trial total-failure arm
Sec 5.3 Table 9: matched governed-vs-ungoverned counterfactual on 2 nodes -- 43 of 50 ungoverned trials leave no record vs 0 of 50 governed, with 95% bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples)

Sec 5.4-5.5: memory-ablation diagnostic explicitly self-flagged as non-independent in one replicate ('rep2 is therefore not an independent replicate') and explicitly labelled 'descriptive counts, not a significance test'
Sec 5.6: reports its own anomaly (summary-arm seed s2 total worker failure) as an unresolved observed failure rather than suppressing it
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: the core governance claim (ledger beats silent-failure baseline) is demonstrated with a real matched counterfactual and bootstrap CIs; the secondary memory-effect claim is explicitly and repeatedly flagged by the author as weaker/descriptive evidence
reproducibilityEvidence: code and all 1,445 trial ledgers released on GitHub with a registered Zenodo DOI; governance metrics explicitly stated to be recomputable from the ledgers without re-running training
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: author repeatedly narrows claim strength to match evidence (e.g. disqualifying rep2, noting the 43/50 figure 'describes these campaigns, not a typical loss rate') -- a rare degree of self-discipline for a single-author paper
candidates.primaryLimitation: single author, task set still research-scale (no production enterprise deployment), and the memory-ablation finding does not reproduce cleanly across replicates
candidates.hiddenAssumption: the 'ungoverned counterfactual' (disabling the pending-trial guard and failure-record appends) is assumed to fairly model what a typical ungoverned agent-experimentation loop actually does in practice
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: if real ungoverned harnesses fail less silently than this matched counterfactual (e.g. because they still log stack traces elsewhere), the 43/50 figure overstates typical information loss; the qualitative point -- that task score alone hides process failures -- would still hold
candidates.presentationReason: explicit separation of established result vs diagnostic probe vs descriptive observation throughout Results section
candidates.reason: the clearest fully-reproducible (full ledger release) demonstration today that task-score-only evaluation of ML/coding agents hides failures that governance infrastructure, not better models, is needed to surface -- a concrete mitigation angle versus the other two selected papers' purely diagnostic framing
